A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMERALD research. All 19 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A.1–A.7, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Crafter experiments, architectural and decoding ablations, and Atari 100k results in Section 4 and Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the Crafter comparisons, ablations and Atari 100k evaluation.

M1.justification: The spatial latent representation, temporal Transformer, MaskGIT predictor, training objectives and actor-critic procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A.4–A.6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Crafter and the same 26 Atari 100k games. No training or evaluation domain, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains DreamerV3 M/XL, Δ-IRIS and human experts. Table 11 retains SimPLe, TWM, IRIS, DreamerV3, STORM, Δ-IRIS and DIAMOND, with the same human and random-policy reference scores.

E3.justification: The 10M-step Crafter budget, 256-episode achievement evaluation, Atari 100k protocol, evaluation metrics and model settings are unchanged, including Table 10.

E4.justification: Both retain the architectural ablations in Table 3, decoding-step analyses in Table 4 and Figures 7–8, reconstruction examples, and appendix achievement curves. No analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Five-seed aggregation, reported return uncertainties and Figure 11's shaded minimum–maximum ranges are unchanged. No run-count disclosure or statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported results match. Table 2 retains EMERALD's 58.1% Crafter score, 16.8 ± 0.6 return and 27 FPS; Table 11 retains its 134% mean and 51% median human-normalized Atari scores. Ablation and achievement results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(11), including world-model losses and actor-critic learning equations, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims: accurate and efficient latent world modeling, exceeding human-expert Crafter scores within 10M steps, and unlocking all 22 achievements.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning spatial detail, temporal memory, decoding accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and Atari performance remain unchanged. Applicability qualifications and the Impact Statement are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-release statement and a link to the burchim/EMERALD GitHub repository in the abstract; v1 supplies no corresponding code-access link. Architecture, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including comparisons with Dreamer, pixel-space world models, TECO and GIT-STORM in Section 2.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-release sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording and section structure are preserved after matching text across page boundaries.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes limited text reflow across columns and page boundaries on pages 1–5. Figures, tables, captions and their contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a direct implementation link absent from v1, modestly improving code discoverability and reproducibility information. The scientific evidence and exposition otherwise remain unchanged; the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.
